msg: CREATE INDEX holds a SHARE lock: every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on the table waits until the index finishes. Safe: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, outside any transaction block.
DROP INDEX takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the table, so reads block too. Safe: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY.
CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block and will abort with error 25001. Safe: move it out of the BEGIN/COMMIT, one statement per migration.
A volatile DEFAULT rewrites every row under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE - the fast path added in PG 11 only covers constant defaults. Safe: add the column with no default, backfill in batches, then SET DEFAULT.
ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL with no DEFAULT fails outright on a table that already has rows (23502). Safe: give it a constant DEFAULT, or add it nullable and SET NOT NULL after a validated CHECK.
UNIQUE on ADD COLUMN builds a unique index while ACCESS EXCLUSIVE is still held, so writes and reads both stop. Safe: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, then ADD CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX.
Changing a column type rewrites the whole table and every index on it under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. Safe: add a new column, backfill in batches, swap the reads, then drop the old column in a later deploy.

SET NOT NULL scans the whole table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. PG 12 and later skip that scan only when a validated CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) already exists. Safe: ADD CONSTRAINT ... CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID, VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, then SET NOT NULL.

A validating FOREIGN KEY locks both tables (ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the child, SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on the parent) while it scans. Safe: ADD CONSTRAINT ... NOT VALID, then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a second statement.
A validating CHECK constraint scans the table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. Safe: ADD CONSTRAINT ... CHECK (...) NOT VALID, then VALIDATE CONSTRAINT, which only needs SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE.
This builds the backing index inside the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. Safe: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY first, then ADD CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX, which only attaches the finished index.

The rename itself is instant, but the old pods are still sending the old name and start erroring at 42703 the moment it commits. Safe: add the new name, write to both, migrate readers, drop the old name a deploy later.

DROP COLUMN is metadata-only, but any SELECT * cached by the still-running old release breaks on commit. Safe: stop referencing the column in a shipped release first (Rails: ignored_columns), then drop it.
VACUUM FULL holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE for the whole rewrite and needs room for a second copy of the table. Safe: leave it out of the migration; use pg_repack or plain VACUUM.
REINDEX blocks writes on the table (and reads on the index) until it finishes. Safe: REINDEX CONCURRENTLY, available since PG 12.
CLUSTER holds ACCESS EXCLUSIVE while it rewrites the table in index order - nothing reads it meanwhile. Safe: do not put CLUSTER in a migration.
TRUNCATE takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE and deletes rows no backfill can bring back. Safe: DELETE in batches with a WHERE, or move the cleanup out of the migration.
LOCK TABLE defaults to ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, the strongest mode there is. Safe: name the weakest mode you actually need (IN SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE MODE) and set a lock_timeout.
An UPDATE with no WHERE takes a row lock on every row in one transaction and blocks writers behind it for the whole run. Safe: loop over primary-key ranges, committing each batch.
DELETE with no WHERE writes a dead tuple for every row and holds them all in one transaction. Safe: delete in batches with a WHERE, or use a partition drop.

No lock_timeout in this migration. If the DDL queues behind one long SELECT, every query that arrives after it queues behind the DDL - that is the outage, not the DDL itself. Safe: SET lock_timeout = '3s'; and retry.
A backfill in the same transaction as the DDL keeps the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock for as long as the backfill runs. Safe: one transaction for the DDL, a separate batched job for the data.
add_index builds the index with a SHARE lock and blocks writes. Safe: add_index ..., algorithm: :concurrently, plus disable_ddl_transaction! on the migration class.
add_reference creates its index the blocking way by default. Safe: add_reference ..., index: false, then add_index with algorithm: :concurrently.
change_column emits ALTER COLUMN TYPE, which rewrites the table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. Safe: new column, batched backfill, swap readers, drop the old one later.
change_column_null(false) emits SET NOT NULL and scans the table. Safe: add a CHECK ... NOT VALID, validate it, then set the column NOT NULL.
Removing a column breaks the release that is still running and still selecting it. Safe: ship self.ignored_columns += [...] first, then remove the column in the next deploy.
A rename breaks every pod of the old release the instant it commits. Safe: add the new name, write to both, move readers, drop the old name in a later migration.
add_foreign_key validates existing rows while holding locks on both tables. Safe: add_foreign_key ..., validate: false, then validate_foreign_key in a second migration.
algorithm: :concurrently inside Rails' automatic transaction aborts with 25001. Safe: add disable_ddl_transaction! at the top of the migration class.
AddIndex emits a plain CREATE INDEX and blocks writes. Safe: AddIndexConcurrently from django.contrib.postgres.operations, with atomic = False on the Migration class.
AlterField can emit ALTER COLUMN TYPE or SET NOT NULL - both scan or rewrite the table under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE. Safe: run sqlmigrate on it first and split the change across two deploys.
A rename breaks the web workers still running the old code. Safe: add the new field, write to both, move readers, then remove the old field.
Removing a field breaks the old release that is still selecting it. Safe: stop referencing it in a shipped release, then remove it in the next migration.
RunPython inside an atomic migration holds every lock the schema operations took for the whole data pass. Safe: atomic = False on the Migration class and commit the backfill in batches.
AddIndexConcurrently in an atomic migration aborts with 25001. Safe: set atomic = False on the Migration class.
